newsitem.title: CUBA: Cubans, tourists warned to be wary of bootleg rum.
newsitem.headline: Cubans, tourists warned to be wary of bootleg rum.

text.p: Cubans, who pride themselves on their rum, were warned on Sunday about imitations that come in bottles with the same labels and aluminium caps as the island's world famous brands.

Sunday's Juventud Rebelde reported the arrest of a gang in Santiago de Cuba that ran a clandestine distillery that produced bottles of "Havana Club Extra Dry," one of Cuba's premier brands, for local consumption and export.
Some of the illegally produced rum is sold by black marketeers to gullible tourists who believe they are getting one of the finest rums in the world at half the price.
Part of the counterfeit rum is also sold in privately owned restaurants and in government-owned bars and eating establishments, the report said.
The police laboratory in Santiago de Cuba claimed the "Havana Club Extra Dry" that was produced by the latest distillery to be shut down was "a wretched adulteration."

Cuban sources said, however, that some of the counterfeit rum sold with big name labels could hardly be distinguished from the original. The article said the illegally produced rum was often mixed with the legitimate draught rums that are sold in bars by employees "in search of easy money."
Internationally renowned brands of Havana cigars are also counterfeited and sold on the street to unsuspecting tourists at one third the price of those made in Cuban factories.
